item.title: Wemby wins NBA West Player of the Week honor after leading Spurs to 3-0 mark
item.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) grabs a rebound at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs center Victor Wembanyama has been named the NBA's Western Conference Player of the Week, marking the fourth time in his career he's received the honor. Boston's Jayson Tatum won the award in the East. Wembanyama helped the Spurs to a 3-0 record for the week ending Sunday, averaging 36.0 points, 10.3 rebounds, 4.3 blocks, 3.7 assists and 2.0 steals in 33.1 minutes while shooting 56.3% from the field. Wembanyama capped the stretch with a 43-point outing in Saturday night's 121-111 victory over Minnesota at the Frost Bank Center. The 22-year-old French superstar dominated in the paint, so much so that he leads the NBA with 23 made alley-oops this season. His 3.8 per game average is more than twice the average of any other player.. "I think that we're doing a better job running the floor, spacing the floor, and I also think he's just doing a better job of asserting himself in the right positions," Spurs forward Julian Champagnie said at shootaround Monday morning when asked about Wembanyama's dominance down low. "I think the intent behind how he's playing is a little different. He's going to dunk the ball a lot more. So the more and more he does that, the more and more that he does his thing in space, it kind of just opens up. Teams have to either guard the three, guard the dunk." The Spurs (4-2) will seek their fifth win in a row when they host Utah (1-5) Monday night at the Frost Bank Center. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: 'A privilege to be here and represent': Astros' Randy Flores on being fifth Latino GM in MLB history
item.description: Randy Flores addresses the media after being introduced as the Houston Astros' new general manager during a press conference in Houston, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) When Randy Flores was asked to answer a question in Spanish at his introductory press conference Monday , he deferred to his father Ron, who was sitting in the front row alongside his wife as well as Flores' wife and three children. As his father cautiously rose from his chair in preparation to handle any Spanish-language questions for his son, the new Houston Astros general manager laughed, "I'm kidding, pop," before telling the assembled media, "My dad is a pastor. He's used to preaching, so he needs to sit down, otherwise you guys will hear a sermon." Flores, who was hired by the Astros on Friday , is just the fifth Latino general manager in the history of Major League Baseball and the first since Cuban-American Al Avila was fired by the Detroit Tigers in 2022. Flores, who asked reporters to call him by his nickname "Flo" since that's how he's known in baseball circles, grew up about 15 miles southeast of Dodger Stadium in Pico Rivera, Calif., where his father, a third-generation Mexican-American raised his family alongside his wife Paula, who died in 2025. "It is a privilege to be here and represent," Flores said when asked about his roots. "If there are any kids out there who are wondering about life in sports and jobs in sports, my hope is that, although I may pass as a güero (fair-skinned), my last name is Flores and I hope that they can aspire to something as well." Flores actually is the Astros' second Latino general manager with Jeff Luhnow, who was born in Mexico City and lived there until he was in the 10th grade, being the first. Avila, Omar Minaya (New York Mets and Montreal Expos) and Ruben Amaro Jr. (Philadelphia Phillies) are the only other Latino general managers in MLB history. Flores' great-great-grandparents immigrated to the United States from northern Mexico and his great-great-grandfather became a pastor in San Antonio, where some of the Flores family still lives. Ron is pastor emeritus at Las Vegas' Meadows Fellowship where his son Ron Jr., who spent three seasons as a reliever for the Oakland Athletics, took over as senior pastor after his father retired. "It's a pleasure to be a part of the Hispanic community here, extending towards San Antonio," Ron Sr., said. "Most of my relatives that live in San Antonio and the surrounding areas are all Houston Astros fans and looking for tickets. I'm looking forward to blessing them. It's been a privilege an a joy to be a part of the community." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Barcelona make major decision on ultras ahead of Aston Villa clash after El Clasico controversy
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona have officially lifted the stadium ban on their primary singing section just in time for the crucial Champions League encounter against Aston Villa. The club had previously imposed a suspension following a series of disciplinary breaches and safety concerns during the high-stakes El Clasico defeat to Real Madrid. Ultras set for return after Clasico fallout Barcelona have confirmed that their designated singing section, known as the 'grada de animacion', will be permitted to return for the upcoming Champions League clash against Aston Villa. In an official statement published on the club's website , Barcelona confirmed that the decision followed a meeting between representatives of the club's security departments and various fan group leaders, resulting in the lifting of a temporary suspension. The ban had previously forced the 1,200-strong group of supporters to miss the recent league fixture against Alaves as punishment for their conduct during the latest encounter with Real Madrid. The internal crackdown followed a formal complaint submitted by La Liga to the disciplinary bodies of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF). The league's report highlighted a toxic atmosphere during the Clasico, documenting multiple instances of objects being hurled onto the pitch, including bottles and lighters. Authorities were particularly concerned by reports of verbal abuse directed at public figures such as Jose Mourinho and Marc Cucurella, which has left the Catalan club facing significant scrutiny and potential further sanctions if the behaviour continues at the Estadi Olimpic Lluis Companys. Security concerns and Camavinga incident FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 One of the most serious allegations contained in the official report involved an attempted physical assault on Real Madrid midfielder Eduardo Camavinga. During the celebrations for Madrid's second goal, a fan allegedly attempted to strike the French international with the mast of a flag. This incident, along with the rain of debris that fell upon the players, served as the primary catalyst for the club’s initial decision to lock out the vocal support group. The club remains wary of the reputational damage these actions cause, as well as the immediate threat to player safety on the pitch. Following the detailed report of ten distinct disciplinary infractions, the fan groups have now formally committed to maintaining a civil and respectful environment for future matches. The club’s decision to reinstate the group is being framed as a vote of confidence, acknowledging the vital role the singing section plays in boosting the team's morale and creating a daunting atmosphere for visiting European sides. item.title: Same Old Problem: UTEP's free throws cost Miner men in opener
item.description: The new-look UTEP basketball team had a quite familiar old problem in its opening 84-76 loss to Northern Kentucky: the Miners still lose games from the free-throw line. Playing against a team that won 20 games last year s a member of the Horizon League, UTEP knocked down 14 of 24 free throws while the Norse made 30-of-33, wiping out a number of things UTEP did well. More: UTEP men's basketball's overhauled roster brings hope, raises questions UTEP trailed most of the game and was within 69-66 inside 4 minutes to go before a five-point NKU run proved more than the Miners could overcome. The North shot 50% to UTEP's 38% and the Miners made 8-of-30 3-pointers, as some other old problems of shooting arose. UTEP also struggled to contain NKU's guards, accounting for much of the 24 Miner fouls. Freshman Youssouf Traore led the Miners with 18 points and six rebounds, Donovan Criss added 13 points and Augusto Cassia had 10 points. UTEP down 4 at half Northern Kentucky closed the first half on a 10-3 run and led 42-38 into the halftime locker room. The Miners struggled on defense, as the Norse shot 56% in the opening 20 minutes. Northern Kentucky also made all 10 of its free-throw attempts while UTEP was 3-of-8, accounting for the difference in the score. Youssouf Traore led the Miners with eight first-half points. Up next UTEP opens its home schedule at the newly rechristened GECU Arena at the Don Haskins Center when it hosts Incarnate Word on Sunday, Nov. 8. item.title: Two Texas Lutheran students killed in car crash near Seguin
item.description: A'Jean Augustine, a Texas Lutheran University football player, was killed in a car crash Monday in Seguin. (Texas Lutheran University) Two Texas Lutheran University students - both of whom played football for the school - were killed in a single-vehicle crash Monday morning near Seguin, police said. A'Jean Augustine, 20, of Houston, and Deyreck Dean, 23, of Rockwall, were killed in the crash, which happened at 2:38 a.m. Monday, officials said. The two men were in a 2012 Kia Sorento SUV that was traveling south on Texas 46 "at a high rate of speed," when the driver lost control, according to police officials. The vehicle crossed into the northbound lanes and struck a guardrail, according to police. In a statement released Monday, the university confirmed the deaths of the two students. "Junior A'Jean (AJ) Augustine of Houston and senior Deyreck Dean of Rockwall, both student athletes, were beloved members of our community and we will long feel the impact of their loss," the university said in the statement. Augustine, a junior from Lamar High School in Houston, was in his third year as a kicker on the Texas Lutheran football team. He was majoring in kinesiology, according to the school's athletics department. Dean played linebacker for four years for Texas Lutheran, from 2022 to 2025, according to the school's athletics department. His major was listed as business management. Texas Lutheran is a Seguin-based private university with about 1,500 students. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Jaylen Warren’s ‘Some Walk, Some Talk’ Cuts Through Jared Verse Noise
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Jaylen Warren delivered the perfect reply to Jared Verse’s pregame noise, proving that actions speak louder than words. The Steelers running back dismissed the Cleveland EDGE rusher’s claims with a simple truth that resonates across the Steel City. This wasn’t just a game; it was a statement sent to anyone who doubts the Black and Gold. The Numbers Tell The Story While the Cleveland defensive end struggled to find his rhythm, Warren found the end zone with ease. The running back logged 143 yards and a touchdown over 17 carries, leading a ground attack that piled up 200 total rushing yards for Pittsburgh. In a match where his team appeared defeated, Verse managed only one tackle and recorded zero sacks. The contrast was stark, and the fans at Acrisure Stadium saw it clearly. Teammates Back The Take Even when Verse tried to block a kick, he crashed headfirst to the turf after Steelers guard Mason McCormick sent him down. McCormick admitted he had no idea who he was hitting, saying, “I really had no idea who it was. Just felt somebody jump,” according to Yahoo Sports . Verse tried to pivot the blame, claiming he was upset about the penalty and that “if this wasn’t football I’d be acting a different way,” per Yahoo Sports. He also noted that he “should have had a better grasp for the type of player I was going up against.” Yet, the team he claimed would take over the Steel City walked away with 27 points. The victory marked Pittsburgh’s fourth consecutive win and gave them a perfect record for October, sending them into their Week 9 bye in first place, as reported by Yahoo Sports. The Browns’ pass rusher remains without a sack through eight games, a stat that makes his pregame boasts look empty. Walking The Walk Cam Heyward summed up the Steelers’ mindset earlier this week when he asked, “Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?” The veteran defensive end added, “But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game,” per BroBible . That attitude is exactly what Verse failed to understand. He spent the buildup challenging Pittsburgh’s offensive front, only to watch them run right through him. The Browns’ defensive end said he “don’t got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty,” yet his own team couldn’t stop the run. Verse promised to “put that one on the calendar” for a rematch, but for now, the Steelers have already won the war of words. The team enters the bye week with the AFC North crown, while Verse must look in the mirror and figure out why he couldn’t stop the walk.

"We're just resetting on our technique, our fundamentals, our communication, making sure we get better at what we can control and not really focusing on others," Ryans said. "That's what the bye week entailed for us. It's a deep look internally." The fourth-year coach said he felt a renewed sense of urgency Monday morning as the Texans entered the first week of November with a 2-5 record, a far cry from what fans were hoping for heading into the season. Ryans said the focus is not on other teams but on themselves and their process to improve, including doing small things to swing margins in their favor. That's going to be key if Houston wants to turn its season around. It's 1-4 in one-score games with all four losses featuring the opponents scoring the game-winning points in the final two minutes of the game or in overtime. Even the one win, the 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, saw the Jaguars score a game-tying field goal with 1:55 left in the game. "How do you find yourself on the winning side of those games?" Ryans said. "It's being great in situational football and it's finishing the proper way. If we do those things, that's when you earn the right to win games." Somehow, despite the disappointing start, Houston is in second place in the AFC South as the Indianapolis Colts are on a four-game losing streak and the Tennessee Titans are 1-7. But Houston has the second-best playoff odds (25%) of all the AFC teams not in the top seven spots heading into this week, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images The moniker Short Game King is under fire after a three-foot putt turned into a career-altering moment during the Internet Invitational. The incident occurred in Episode 2 of the tournament, where the stakes were far higher than a typical online challenge. Team Blue faced elimination after a string of missed opportunities that included critical errors from both SGK and his partner, Roger Steele. item.title: Brewers fans flock to Raising Cane's to meet Yelich. Only a few did.
item.description: Mark Anderson left his house in Racine shortly after 10 p.m. Nov. 1 to go to Raising Cane's. Instead of driving south to the closer location in Kenosha, he headed north to Greendale, arriving at 11 p.m. The restaurant did not close until 2 a.m. the next day, so Anderson had ample time to get some food. But he stayed in his car, wanting to wait to order his box combo until the next day. When he could get it from Christian Yelich. The Milwaukee Brewers captain was slated to appear at Raising Cane's in Greendale, 5250 S. 76th St., for a "victory shift," his latest celebrity appearance after helping the Brewers win their first World Series title on Oct. 28. Anderson, 34, was not missing this opportunity. Even if it meant waiting 12 hours for his food. Even if it meant sleeping in his car − or trying to, anyway. Even if it meant leaving his car at 4 a.m. and waiting in line in the cold for seven hours. Anderson, wearing a World Series sweatshirt and baseball cap, ordered and received his food from Yelich just after 11 a.m. on Nov. 2, perhaps the longest someone has waited for a Cane's meal. Was it worth it? "Absolutely," he said. "Food's delicious. And... "... it's Christian Yelich." Anderson might have been the first to arrive, but he was the second person in line. Mathew Zimmer beat him to the door. Zimmer, 19, set his alarm for 2:30 a.m., left his house at 3:30 a.m. and arrived at Cane's by 4. He took a chair from the restaurant's outdoor seating area so he didn't have to stand. He wore a Brewers 2026 City Connect jersey with Yelich's name and number on the back, and a Cheesehead top hat which sat atop a Brewers cap underneath. "I wanted to get the chance to meet Christian Yelich," Zimmer said. "You're meeting a world champion." At 11:11 a.m., after Yelich did a news conference and filmed promotional content for Raising Cane's, Zimmer did. The first person to order from Yelich, Zimmer got a box combo with a lemonade. He made his way to the back of the restaurant and took his first bites. This was the first time he ever ate Cane's in his life, and he got it from Yelich. "It's perfect," Zimmer said. "Two-for-one." After getting his meal, Zimmer showed Yelich a video from the Brewers championship parade three days prior. In it, Zimmer got Yelich's attention as he drove past on a bus and threw the designated hitter his phone. Yelich caught it, flipped the camera around and took a selfie video before finding Zimmer in the crowd − thanks to the top hat − and tossing the phone back. Yelich remembered the interaction, telling Zimmer he was the only person he did that with. Only five fans got served by Yelich, who spent more time filming content Zimmer and Anderson were the most dedicated people, but not the only ones who showed up early. item.description: Ricardo Pepi has 42 U.S. Men's National Team appearances to his name -Credit:John Dorton/USSF, Getty Images U.S. Men's National Team forward Ricardo Pepi made his comeback from a nearly two-month injury layoff with a goal and an assist as a substitute in PSV's 7-0 domestic rout of Willem II. Pepi, recovering from a muscle problem, appears poised to receive a call-up to the USMNT camp ahead of the team's CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal double-header against Haiti. The 23-year-old, already a 2026 FIFA World Cup representative with 42 caps to his name, was absent from an impressive September camp that witnessed Cavan Sullivan and other American prospects net their maiden international goals. Pepi, who came through the FC Dallas academy system, spoke exclusively to The Mirror US Sport about monitoring Sullivan's strike against Mexico. -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images The PSV player discussed the future trajectory of the USMNT, his latest discussions with manager Mauricio Pochettino, the contrasts between Dutch and American soccer traditions, and the significance of his continued UEFA Champions League participation. item.description: Texas State fans cheer during the I-35 rivalry college football game against UTSA at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 12, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) The Pac-12 released a statement last Friday condemning the discriminatory chants toward the Church of Latter-day Saints that occurred during the Texas State football game against Utah State. The broadcast from the game at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos picked up audio of fans chanting "F--- the mormons." Scott Gerard, Utah State's play-by-play broadcaster, said on social media that he'd heard the chants. "On Saturday, Oct. 24, the Pac-12 was notified of religiously discriminatory conduct directed at Utah State student-athletes and fans during Texas State's home football game," the Pac-12 statement reads. "There is no place for such behavior in any venue, nor should it be tolerated. The league has reviewed the preventive measures in place at both instances at Pac-12 venues this season, and will be working with its Board of Directors to strengthen fan conduct standards and accountability, both to prevent this behavior at our own games and to better protect our student-athletes and fans across any sporting events." Students roam campus at Texas State University in San Marcos Monday, June 30, 2025. The university announced they joined the Pac-12 conference Monday. (Mikala Compton/American-Statesman) A Texas State spokesperson has not immediately replied to a request for a statement via email or text. Similar derogatory jeers were heard during the BYU-UCF game last week and during the BYU-Colorado State game in Week 3. Colorado State apologized a day after the game, stating that "mocking anyone's faith has no place at CSU." The Big 12 fined UCF $100,000 for its fans' actions and established a conference-wide policy with "escalating consequences for discriminatory conduct." A first offense leads to a $100,000. A second in the same game results in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and possibly a $500,000 fine, according to the Big 12. item.description: Serie A | Atalanta 0-3 Parma: Gilardino gets first win as Daffara frustrates Sarri’s side Giovanni Fabbian, a Davide Zappacosta own goal and Simone Lontani’s long-range strike gave Parma a shock 3-0 win at Atalanta, Alberto Gilardino’s first since taking charge. Atalanta went into the game 11th in Serie A on 11 points. They hadn’t won at home since beating Venezia on 12 October, and had drawn 2-2 at Fiorentina on Thursday. Maurizio Sarri’s side are in the middle of an injury crisis, with only 19 players called up. Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen joined Raoul Bellanova, Gianluca Scamacca, Giacomo Raspadori, Sead Kolašinac, Franck Kessié, Isak Hien, Odilon Kossounou and Pompei on the sidelines, while Giorgio Scalvini returned in defence. Parma were in the bottom three on five points after a 0-0 draw with Udinese, still waiting for Gilardino’s first win. They were without Adrián Bernabé, who picked up a muscle problem in training on Sunday, so Fabbian started in midfield and Lontani up front alongside El Bilal Touré. Atalanta dominated the opening half hour, with 73% possession. Charles De Ketelaere was the main threat: he dragged an early effort wide, forced Giovanni Daffara into a save at his near post, then fired just past the far post after weaving through the defence. Ederson whistled a long-range drive inches wide, and Nikola Krstović scuffed a shot past the post. Parma’s first real chance came from a set piece, when Enrico Delprato headed wide from Vincent Sierro’s corner. They didn’t waste the next one. Sierro swung in another corner on 41 minutes, and Fabbian headed home from close range. Daffara made a sharp save to deny Nicola Zalewski just before half-time. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Atalanta seal their fate with dismal second half against Parma Things got worse for Atalanta two minutes after the restart. Zappacosta stretched to cut out a cross and diverted it inside his own left post. Jonathan Rowe wasted two good chances to pull one back. On 58 minutes, Fabbian teed up Lontani, who curled a superb shot from outside the area into the bottom-right corner. Sarri brought on Eljif Elmas, Kamaldeen Sulemana, Lazar Samardžić and Javison Idele, but Daffara was in inspired form. He produced a fine save to keep out Krstović’s low drive, and Mario Pašalić headed against the crossbar from close range. item.title: Baun’s Big Play Won’t Fix Eagles’ Offensive Woes
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Eagles needed a miracle on Sunday, and they got one from Zack Baun, according to DAZN . The linebacker scooped up a loose ball and gave his team a fresh set of downs right at the Commanders’ 26-yard line. But the final score tells a different story. Philadelphia only managed 10 points while Washington took home 27. That single play did not save the offense. The team capitalized on the mistake by Chig Okonkwo to find itself in a strong position, per DAZN. Yet the Eagles could not convert that advantage into points. They walked off the field with nothing to show for it. A great defensive stop means little if the offense cannot finish the drive. The Field Position Trap Starting at the 26-yard line is as close as you can get without actually touching the end zone. NFL.com reported that Baun’s recovery gave the Eagles a fresh possession starting at the Commanders’ 26-yard line. That is prime territory for a touchdown. The defense worked hard to get the ball back. The offense failed to use it. Fans saw the ball land right in the hands of a key player. The hope was that the momentum would shift instantly. Instead, the game slipped further away. The Eagles had the chance to cut the lead or take the lead. They chose to go nowhere. Defense Wins, Offense Loses The defense did its job by forcing the turnover. Andrew Mukuba forced the fumble that led to the recovery. That is a key play in any football game. But one play cannot fix a broken offense. The team scored only 10 points in the entire game. That is not enough to beat a team like Washington. Philadelphia needs more than just a lucky break. They need a plan that works when the ball is on the ground. The fumble recovery by Zack Baun gave the Eagles a fresh possession, but the result was the same. The team failed to score after the first quarter. The defense deserves credit for the effort, but the offense must step up. The next game is against the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8. The clock is ticking for this team to find answers. They cannot rely on the defense to bail them out every week. The Giants will be ready to fight at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles must show they can score when they get the ball back. Stats Box Final Score: Washington Commanders 27, Philadelphia Eagles 10.
